question:
The ones who explain, don't wait here.

The ones who learn, don't wait here either.

Yet something belonging to the first group

waits here for its next move.

It asks not for fuel, but for a little time connected to power.

Find where it waits.

Metal, machines and minds meet here.

I am not a classroom, yet learning happens.

I am not the arena, yet I stand beside one.

Find the place where engineers make things,

where once memories were made but now rarely visited by the same people who made those memories.

I was not here for long,

yet many will soon know me well.

I don't speak, but I can give you

exactly what you ask for.

No person stands behind me,

yet something warm comes from within.

Find the newest member of the campus.

Your next clue is with someone nearby.
Find the volunteer and complete a small fun challenge to receive it!

Challenge may be a quick task, a dialogue, a fun question, or a simple dare. 😄

D has a successor. Find it.

Once you do, don't face it.

What you seek is hidden from the usual view.

Leave the familiar side behind,

take the longer way around,

and discover what waits where the building

keeps its secrets.

Every circle has a point where it begins.
You have travelled far enough to complete yours.
Find the point that has seen you before—
only then is your journey whole. 🔍

A: “Is your machine working?”
B: “Yes.”
A: “Who switches it on?”
B: “Nobody.”
A: “Then who powers it?”
B: “Look up.”
A: “Where do I start?”
B: “525.”
A: “525?”
B: “Find the one vehicle that comes when people need help.”

Look for the wall where
poverty meets education,
health meets climate,
and peace meets partnership.
There are many colours,
but only one number matters.
Count carefully they are 17

No photograph was taken. No name was written. But every arrival was accounted for. THE QUESTION If nothing happened, why was someone watching?

🌳 I stand among the trees.
🪨 I rest among the rocks.
🚀 My thoughts reached beyond the sky.
🎵 My words ask you to hear what others miss.
Who am I?

When everything goes wrong,
there is a special way marked for you to leave safely.
Think of the two words used on that sign.
The first word describes the situation.
The second word tells you what you should do.
Now:
Take the first letter of the first word.
Count the letters in the second word.
First letter → Where
Number → Which floor
Put them together to find your next destination.
Where are you going?

I speak without a voice.
I teach without a classroom.
I can inspire without knowing your name.
Many words stand together,
but none of them belong to a conversation.
Look for the place where someone's words are waiting to be read.
